newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LE TISSIER GIVES SAINTS DRAW WITH LAST-GASP STRIKE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LE TISSIER GIVES SAINTS DRAW WITH LAST-GASP STRIKE.

text.p: Kenny Dalglish's reign as Newcastle manager began on a disappointing note on Saturday when his new team conceded two goals in the last two minutes to be held 2-2 by Southampton at The Dell and lose ground in the hunt for the English title.

Newcastle, who also let a 2-0 lead slip last week against Aston Villa, seemed to have all three points secured when Lee Clark put them 2-0 up with an 82nd minute goal. Les Ferdinand had scored the first after 14 minutes.
But an 88th minute goal from Neil Maddison and a last-gasp screaming drive from Matt Le Tissier gave Southampton an unlikely draw.

Newcastle slipped to seven points behind Liverpool after Liverpool beat Aston Villa 3-0 at Anfield where locally-born 18-year-old Jamie Carragher scored with a 50th minute header on his full debut. Stan Collymore got the second and Robbie Fowler added the third.
Second-placed Manchester United won 2-0 at Coventry to stay two points behind Liverpool.

There were mixed fortunes for the bottom club Middlesbrough, who ended Sheffield Wednesday's 13-match unbeaten run with a 4-2 home win. Italian Fabrizio Ravanelli opened the scoring with a 14th minute penalty, but then was sent off after 70 minutes after picking up a second booking.
